## 🔴 Critical launch-crash fix — read this first if you are on v1.13.0, v1.14.0, or v1.14.1

**Those three versions crash on launch on macOS** (`SIGABRT`, a second or two after
the icon bounces, usually before the window draws). **v1.14.2 fixes it.**

**If you are on one of those versions you cannot update from inside the app** — it
aborts before you can click the Update button. Reinstall instead:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://chatoss.ai/install.sh | sh
```

…or download `ChatOSS_1.14.2_universal.dmg` below and drag it to `/Applications`.
Your data is untouched — conversations, boards, projects, and settings all live in
`~/Library/Application Support/com.chatoss.desktop` and are not affected.

Already on v1.12.0 or earlier? You were never hit by this, and the in-app Update
button works normally.

---

### What was wrong

The `chatoss launch` feature (added in v1.13.0) starts a local model-redirect
server during app startup, and that bootstrap looked up its handles as Tauri
managed state — but the state was never registered with `.manage()`. Tauri's
`state()` **panics** when a type was never managed, and Tauri runs the `setup`
hook inside macOS's `applicationDidFinishLaunching:`, an Objective-C callback a
Rust panic cannot unwind out of. So the panic turned straight into `abort()`:

```
state() called before manage() for chat_oss::launch::LaunchServerState
```

The crash landed a second or two into launch because startup does database and
migration work before reaching that line — which is why it read as random rather
than as a hard, every-time failure.

### Fixed in this release

- **The app launches again.** The managed state is registered, and the startup
  bootstrap now resolves it without a panicking call, so a missing registration
  can never abort launch again.
- **`chatoss launch` actually works.** It was entirely dead in v1.13.0–v1.14.1:
  the local server never bound a port and never wrote its port file, so the
  `chatoss` CLI could never find the running app. It now starts on app launch and
  serves `claude-code`, `opencode`, and `codex` redirects as designed.
- **Regression tests** now assert both invariants (the state is registered, and
  the bootstrap never uses the panicking lookup), so this cannot come back
  unnoticed.

### Platforms

macOS universal (Apple Silicon + Intel), Windows x64, Linux x86_64.
